items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: I ended up getting like a guitar scholarship that Mundell Lowe was paying for

ctx.x: What did you get accepted as, and what got you in there? Your compositions?

No. It’s not like, I mean back then, and we’re talking ’75, it was a state university, I mean it still is for that matter. But it wasn’t — the whole financial outlay was much less. I remember even then a semester was something between eight and twelve hundred bucks, for a semester’s worth of classes. A full load. And roughly the dorm was probably about the same. And after my first year there I ended up getting like a guitar scholarship that Mundell Lowe was paying for, it was like a hundred bucks a semester but…
know if I decide to use my brain it’s going to come out okay, so in high school I wasn’t using my brain so much but what the heck.
